head.title: Separate decisions from progress, and attach evidence to finished work
head.subtitle: Readers see what needs their answer apart from what the agent tracks; finished steps can show their proof without losing approval.
head.tldr: Seven steps. Checklists become either a **decision list** (needs your answer) or a **progress list** (the agent tracks it), never both; the build rejects a mix. Steps and progress items gain an optional `evidence` list, embedded or linked, that keeps a plan approved like `status: done` does. Four questions need a pick.

items.md: A checklist whose every item has `choices`. The reader answers it; the answers go with Send answers, Approve or Request changes.
A checklist with no `choices` on any item: procedure steps, verification checks, follow-ups. Ticks track work.
What shows a step or progress item worked: **embedded** (text, a command and its output, an image beside the doc) or **linked** (a file path or URL).

items.title: Classify checklists and reject mixed ones in `build.py`
items.md: Add `checklist_kind(b)` → `decisions` or `progress` from its items. A list with both kinds is an error on a new rev and a warning on older ones (`contract_level`, `build.py:1733`). Nested checklists are classified on their own. Per question 1, also lint the placement of decision lists. Split `acme-status` `next/next` into a decision list and a progress list.

items.title: Render decision lists and progress lists as two kinds
items.md: In `renderChecklist` (`template.html:2862`): a decision list gets a question icon, a **Needs your answer** label and an `N open` count in place of the bar. A progress list keeps the bar and gets a one-line caption: on plans *“The agent marks these as work lands; ticking doesn't change approval”*, elsewhere *“Your own tracker”*. The Send answers and Approve Markdown list decisions before ticks (`decisionsMd`, `answerItems`).

items.title: Handle a pick changed on an approved plan
items.md: Per question 3. Applies to plan, design, presentation and website pages (`APPROVABLE`). Earlier revisions and compare view already disable pills.

items.title: Validate `evidence` and count it as progress
items.md: Each entry: `label` (required) plus at least one of `md`, `code`/`lang`, `src` (a file beside the doc, checked like a media `src`), `href` (a path or `http(s)` URL, checked like inline links). Error on a decision item. Pop `evidence` in `without_progress` for steps and progress items, so `patch step:… --set status=done --json '{"evidence": […]}'` keeps the approval.

items.title: Show evidence on steps and progress items
items.md: In `renderSteps` (`template.html:2710`) and the checklist item body: an **Evidence** group. Embedded entries render inline (md, a code block with Copy, an image or video); linked ones render as a chip tagged *linked* that opens the path or URL. A step with evidence shows a small evidence count in its meta row. Compare view gets an **Evidence** row in *What changed*; Copy checklist adds evidence links under the item.

The mix error breaks a user's existing doc on its next rev
Build fails until the list is split
Error names both item ids and the fix; older revs only warn
An agent rewrites scope inside an evidence note

f1858c6af90ca292.md:
- **Mixed lists.** An item becomes a decision only by having `choices` (`skills/bluedoc/scripts/build.py:1915-1940`). Both kinds share one header, one `n of m` count and one bar (`skills/bluedoc/assets/template.html:3012-3016`). Of the 17 checklists in the examples and skeletons, one mixes them: `acme-status` `next/next` (1 decision, 2 actions).
- **Approval carry.** `without_progress` strips step `status`, checklist `done` and the approved `choice` before comparing revs (`build.py:758-786`). `approval_carries` compares the rest (`build.py:789-802`). Anything else on a step, a note or a link, asks for approval again.
- **No evidence field.** A step has `md`, `files`, `refs`, `status` and `effort` (`references/schema.md:228-238`). A checklist item has `verify`, which is the planned check, not its result.
- **Picks after approval.** The page still lets the reader click another pill on an approved plan. That pick stays in reader state until a later Request changes sends it. The chip stays green meanwhile.

items.text: How does a checklist say which kind it is?
items.sub: Recommend inferring it: no new field, no migration, stored ticks and picks keep their keys.

choices.label: Inferred from items
choices.md: All items have `choices`: a decision list. None do: a progress list. Both: build error.

choices.label: Explicit `kind` field
choices.md: `"kind": "decisions" | "progress"` on the block; every existing checklist gets one.

items.detail: **Inferred** changes no JSON outside `acme-status`. **Explicit** reads clearer in the JSON and catches an author who forgot `choices` on one question, at the cost of migrating 17 checklists and the skeletons.

items.text: How do decision lists get priority on the page?
items.sub: Recommend a header chip plus a lint: the author keeps section order, the reader can't miss open questions.

choices.label: Header chip + lint
choices.md: A chip under the title, “N questions need your answer”, jumps to the first open one. The build warns when a decision list follows a progress list.

choices.label: Page moves them first
choices.md: The page renders decision sections above all others, whatever the JSON order.

choices.label: Lint only
choices.md: Only the build warning; no page change.

items.detail: **Reorder** breaks a review doc, where each finding's decision sits in its PR's section, and makes the page order differ from the JSON. **Lint only** leaves review pages and long docs without a visible prompt.

items.text: What happens when the reader changes a pick on an approved plan?
items.sub: Recommend flagging it: no locked controls, and the agent hears about it.

choices.label: Flag it, ask to send
choices.md: The chip turns amber, “Pick changed since approval”, and Request changes lights up with the pick.

choices.label: Lock the pills
choices.md: Pills are disabled on the approved rev; the reader comments and sends Request changes to reopen.

items.detail: **Flag** keeps one way to change your mind, the same as before approval. **Lock** prevents a stray click from diverging silently, but changing a pick then takes a comment and an extra round.

items.text: Should linked local evidence files be fingerprinted?
items.sub: Recommend link only: optional evidence shouldn't add history machinery; embedded is the tamper-proof form.

choices.label: Link only
choices.md: A linked path or URL is a pointer, tagged *linked* on the page; it may change after the step is done.

choices.label: Hash local files
choices.md: The build records each linked local file's sha256 in the revision; the page marks one that changed since.

items.detail: **Hash** costs a history field per revision, a check per render, and a new compare state. URLs can't be hashed either way.
